title: UAV-X human preflight receipt
description: Round 3 finding 4 made registration and eligibility block the loop. Round 4 finding 7 found the block was shallow: preflight checked three fields and let a plausible-looking partial file through, and nothing ever read the delivery budget it recorded, so an oversized package could reach the send step with no accepted route. Every field here is one a human has to go and do, and the dates make a claim checkable later. See stage-1/human-preflight.md.

done.description: Date registered on techfest.org. There is no submission portal, so registration is the only thing tying this email to an entry.

email.description: The registered address. The submission has to come from it.

competition_id.description: The id Techfest issues on registration, UAVX- followed by 12 upper case hex characters. Added 1 September, when the first one arrived. The two fields beside it are things a person types, and a date and an address can both be typed by somebody who never registered. This one cannot be guessed, so it is the only part of this block that is evidence rather than a claim. The organisers can also be asked to confirm it, which is the point of recording it rather than trusting the date.

declaration.description: Explicit statement of no attachment to the PUSHPAK Project, the Drone Centre, or IIT Bombay, IISER Bhopal and VJTI Mumbai. This disqualifies at any stage, including after Stage 1 results.

done.description: Date the UAV-X WhatsApp group was joined. Organiser clarifications land there first.

last_checked.description: When the WhatsApp group was last read. The rules say changes are communicated through official channels, and round 5 finding 8 is right that an API diff does not read a channel. The final package check refuses a stale one.

fallback.description: What is assumed while the answers are pending. Source delivery method and video length both change work, so neither can wait for a reply that may not come.

last_checked.description: When the reply inbox was last read for organiser answers.

attachment_limit_mb.description: What the mail provider actually allows. The final package check totals the attachment manifest against this.

route.description: How the package gets there: attachments, a repository link, a shared drive link, or a split archive.

fallback.description: What happens if the organisers say attachments only and the package is over budget.

compliance_review.description: Round 5 finding 9: the old package check searched the proposal for the six letters 'regulat', which a sentence saying the system is unregulated would satisfy. A machine can check that the citations are present and resolve; only a person can say the analysis is right, so a person signs it.

statement.description: What was checked and what it concluded. Stage 1 and Stage 2 are simulation only, so no permission is needed now; the obligations that would attach before any physical flight are the point of writing it down.
